# Config and environment reference

This page is the operator and integrator lookup surface for the configuration
families that are exposed in the current repository. Use it as the fast index,
then move into the deeper runtime docs when you need subsystem detail.

## At a glance

| Family | Representative settings | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local ports and launch | `CALIBER_PORT`, `MLFLOW_PORT`, `MLFLOW_GATEWAY_PORT` | bringing up the local suite |
| Core runtime | `CALIBER_DATABASE_URL`, `CALIBER_LOG_SINK` | wiring the control plane and logging |
| Access and auth | `CALIBER_AUTH_MODE`, `CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS`, `CALIBER_CSRF_ENABLED` | who may sign in and what each user may do |
| LLM provider and gateway | `CALIBER_LLM_PROVIDER`, `CALIBER_LLM_BASE_URL` | choosing provider routing |
| Release path | `CALIBER_PROMOTER_PROVIDER`, `CALIBER_ARTIFACT_STORE_PROVIDER`, `CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER`, `CALIBER_ALLOW_SIMULATED_PROVIDERS` | choosing whether Apply performs a real MLflow release (the default) and whether evaluation scores are real |
| Object store | `CALIBER_OBJECT_STORE_*` | uploads, extraction, previews, log mirroring |
| Workflow storage | `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_STORAGE_*` | run workspaces, limits, retention, signed URLs |
| Event backend | `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_EVENT_BACKEND` | workflow queue and runtime eventing |
| Feature flags | `CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA`, `CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS`, `CALIBER_FEATURE_COOKBOOKS`, `CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES` | turning on the preview, record-only and experimental areas the alpha leaves off |

## Reference

## 1. Local launch and ports

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_PORT` | host port for the CALIBER UI/API service |
| `MLFLOW_PORT` | host port for the MLflow UI; `start.sh` guards common collisions |
| `MLFLOW_GATEWAY_PORT` | host port for the MLflow AI Gateway surface |

## 2. Core runtime

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_DATABASE_URL` | SQLAlchemy URL for the CALIBER metadata store; `sqlite:///./caliber.db` when unset. The server never creates its own tables: run `caliber-migrate` before the first start and after every upgrade |
| `CALIBER_LOG_SINK` | `s3` (the default) keeps stderr and mirrors JSONL to the object store when available; `stderr` disables the mirroring |
| `CALIBER_STATIC_PREFIX` | serve behind a reverse-proxy prefix when applicable |

## 3. LLM and gateway

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_LLM_PROVIDER` | select the default provider implementation; `fake` (a deterministic stub) when unset, `openai` needs the `llm` extra |
| `CALIBER_LLM_DIAGNOSIS_MODEL` | default OpenAI model; `gpt-5.6-luna` when unset |
| `CALIBER_LLM_REASONING_EFFORT` | platform-wide reasoning default; `high` when unset |
| `CALIBER_GEPA_REFLECTION_MODEL` | GEPA reflection model; inherits the Luna default |
| `CALIBER_MEMORY_LLM_MODEL` | memory extraction model; inherits the Luna default |
| `CALIBER_LLM_BASE_URL` | override the OpenAI-compatible base URL |
| `CALIBER_GATEWAY_URI` | discover an MLflow AI Gateway surface |
| `CALIBER_PROMOTER_PROVIDER` | `mlflow` (default) registers a new prompt version and moves the live alias on Apply; `fake` only simulates and needs the opt-in below |
| `CALIBER_ARTIFACT_STORE_PROVIDER` | `mlflow` (default) reads prompts from the registry; `fake` needs the opt-in below |
| `CALIBER_EVAL_PROVIDER` | `fake` (the default) returns canned scores that are marked `simulated` everywhere they are shown or stored; `mlflow` wraps `mlflow.genai.evaluate` |
| `CALIBER_ALLOW_SIMULATED_PROVIDERS` | set `true` to permit a `fake` promoter or artifact store, or a real LLM provider combined with the `fake` evaluator (tests, demos); startup refuses each of those otherwise, and every simulated Apply is marked `simulated` |

The assistant uses the same OpenAI default through `CALIBER_ASSISTANT_MODEL`
and `CALIBER_ASSISTANT_REASONING`. Explicit per-asset and per-call selections
remain supported overrides.

## 6. Event backend

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_EVENT_BACKEND` | `in_process` (the default), `database`, `nats` or `redis` |
| `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED` | `false` by default; the run queue that wait and human-approval nodes need, together with `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_RUN_CHECKPOINTING_ENABLED` |

## 7. Access and auth

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_PROFILE` | `development` (the default: start with whatever is set) or `reference` (refuse to start while any setting breaks the reference deployment: a SQLite database, CSRF off, the dev identity fallback, the `admin/admin` bootstrap, `trusted_header` without a proxy secret, egress policy off, plain-HTTP MCP, self-approval, an armed fault barrier; every violation is listed with the variable to change) |
| `CALIBER_FAULT_BARRIERS` | Test only. A comma list of fault-barrier names (`before_dispatch`, `after_downstream_commit`, `before_receipt_persist`, `after_outbox_commit`, `after_evaluation_claim`); a process that reaches an armed barrier exits at once with status 137, like a crash, so the scenario tests can kill a worker at an exact point. Unset (the default) makes every barrier a no-op. The `reference` profile refuses to start while it is set. Not a setting in `CaliberConfig`: it is read straight from the environment. |
| `CALIBER_AUTH_MODE` | `session` (the default: server-side sessions and personal access tokens) or `trusted_header` (trusts `X-CALIBER-User`; only behind a proxy) |
| `CALIBER_ADMIN_USERS`, `CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS`, `CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS` | comma-separated user ids granted `caliber.admin`, `caliber.operator` and `caliber.approver`; all empty by default, so a first login is a viewer. These are global scopes, not project roles, and `caliber.admin` is not an implicit project member |
| `CALIBER_CSRF_ENABLED` | `false` by default; when `true`, every `POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT` and `DELETE` (bearer-token calls included) needs an `X-CALIBER-CSRF` token, signed with the secret named by `CALIBER_CSRF_SIGNING_SECRET_ENV` and valid for `CALIBER_CSRF_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` (3600 by default) |
| `CALIBER_REFERENCE_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `1048576` (1 MiB) by default. Under `CALIBER_PROFILE=reference` only: the largest request body accepted, enforced on the declared `Content-Length` and on the bytes actually streamed (a chunked or understated body is bounded too); a larger one gets `413` with `{"reason": "request_too_large", "max_bytes": N}`. The development profile installs no limit. |
| `CALIBER_REFERENCE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `268435456` (256 MiB) by default. Under `CALIBER_PROFILE=reference` only: the largest `multipart/form-data` request body accepted (the file-upload routes), which replaces `CALIBER_REFERENCE_MAX_BODY_BYTES` for those requests when larger. Raise it together with `CALIBER_WORKFLOW_STORAGE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`. A larger body gets `413`. The GitHub webhook route keeps its own `CALIBER_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES`. |
| `CALIBER_EXECUTION_LEASE_SECONDS` | `30` by default (3 to 3600). Reference profile only: how long the execution-owner lease lasts. The process that holds it runs the background loops and renews it every third of this; a process that cannot renew stops the loops (`/readiness` `execution_role` becomes `secondary`), and when the holder dies a secondary becomes the owner within about this long. Every other process serves HTTP only. |
| `CALIBER_EFFECT_RECONCILER_ENABLED` | `true` by default. Reference profile only: run the effect reconciler loop in the execution owner. It asks each connector bound in `CALIBER_EFFECT_CALLBACK_CONNECTORS` about the effects nobody recorded the outcome of, by their logical key, and records `unknown` for a dispatch stuck in flight; it never re-sends an effect. Turn it off only if another process under the same lease does that work: without it an effect whose settle failed stays blocked until an operator reconciles it. See [The reconciler loop](m-64-reference-profile.md#the-reconciler-loop-and-the-in-flight-rule-b055d-997). |
| `CALIBER_EFFECT_RECONCILER_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `15` by default (1 to 3600). Seconds between reconciler passes. |
| `CALIBER_EFFECT_RECONCILER_BUDGET_SECONDS` | `20` by default (1 to 600). A pass stops starting lookups after this long; a lookup in progress finishes (its own timeout applies) and the next pass continues after the last proposal it looked at. |
| `CALIBER_EFFECT_IN_FLIGHT_MAX_SECONDS` | `900` by default (300 to 86400). How long an effect may stay `dispatched` under the lease that is still current before the loop records it `unknown` and asks the downstream. It **must exceed the longest a dispatch can legitimately take**: the executor's timeout (30 s by default) times its attempts (at most 5), its backoff (under 4 s) and the receipt lookup (30 s) come to about 3 minutes with the defaults, which the 300 s floor covers. A connector configured with a longer timeout needs a larger value; a dispatcher that is merely slow finds its row `unknown` and the reconciler settles it by lookup instead. |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TURNS` | `25` by default (1 to 1000). The most provider turns one governed agent step may be given; a step's own limit is capped at this before it runs. See [Central step limits](m-64-reference-profile.md#central-step-limits-turns-tool-calls-tokens-and-the-deadline-b083-752). |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` | `50` by default (0 to 1000). The most read-tool calls one governed agent step may make; the platform counts them and refuses the one past the limit. `0` allows none. |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_TOKENS` | `200000` by default (1 to 10000000). The most tokens (prompt plus completion) one governed agent step may use. |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_MAX_SECONDS` | `600` by default (1 to 86400, finite). The longest window from the moment a governed agent step is asked that its deadline may reach; a later deadline is brought forward to it. |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_RUN_MAX_TOKENS` | `2000000` by default (1 to 1000000000). The most tokens one run's governed agent steps may reserve and be charged in total. A step's `max_tokens` ceiling is reserved against it, under the run's row lock, before the adapter is called; a step that would take the run past it is refused (`token_budget_exhausted`) and its adapter is never called. A ceiling larger than the whole budget refuses every step. See [Token reservations](m-64-reference-profile.md#token-reservations-reserved-before-the-call-charged-conservatively-settled-once-b084-761). |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_RESERVATION_GRACE_SECONDS` | `300` by default (1 to 86400, finite). How long past its step's deadline an open token reservation (a worker died or was cancelled mid-call) is left before the execution owner's reconciler loop finalizes it as `abandoned`, at its whole reservation: a reservation is never released, so this only moves when the row stops being open. |
| `CALIBER_AGENT_STEP_TOOL_BACKENDS` | `[]` by default. A JSON array of the registered tools whose protected action a governed agent step may propose (#1051): each row is `{"tool": <registry name>, "version": <registry version>, "backend": "document_request"}`. This is the trusted map from a tool's registry identity to the backend its effect is sent through; a manifest, a tool call and a model cannot write it. In the reference profile an agent node bound to a mapped tool runs as a governed step (its protected action becomes an approvable proposal, sent once after the exact approval, under the execution-owner lease); every other agent node runs as before. Empty governs no agent node. Only `document_request` is accepted, the one backend with an authoritative lookup by key. The downstream is the `base_url` of that connector's binding in `CALIBER_EFFECT_CALLBACK_CONNECTORS` for the run's project; a mapped tool with no binding is refused before anything is claimed. See [Reference profile](m-64-reference-profile.md#the-worker-binds-the-governed-path-1051). |
| `CALIBER_EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED` | `false` by default; always on under `CALIBER_PROFILE=reference`. Record every run event in the transactional outbox in the same transaction as the event and deliver it (at least once) to the registered consumers; see [Events: the outbox](m-64-reference-profile.md#events-the-outbox). |
| `CALIBER_EVENT_OUTBOX_POLL_SECONDS` | `1` by default (0.05 to 60). How long the publisher waits when nothing is due. |
| `CALIBER_EVENT_OUTBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `20` by default (1 to 1000). Delivery attempts before an event is marked `dead` and kept for an operator. |
| `CALIBER_EVENT_OUTBOX_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` by default (0 to 3650). How long delivered events are kept before they are pruned. |
| `CALIBER_ADMISSION_ENABLED` | `false` by default; always on under `CALIBER_PROFILE=reference`. Admit every run a user starts (the create-run route, the event trigger and the assistant's run tool), and admit scheduler/service-token runs through server-created typed service principals: resolve and pin everything the run depends on, issue its grant, decide it under the policy and store its immutable run manifest in the transaction that creates the run (see [Admitting a run](m-64-reference-profile.md#admitting-a-run-b022a-680)). A refusal stores nothing. Scheduler/service-token lineage is resolved from the deployment's persisted environment class and exactly one active environment with a current release; there is no `prod` or sole-row fallback. Off elsewhere, scheduler/service paths remain explicitly labelled legacy and user paths retain their existing legacy behavior. |
| `CALIBER_ADMISSION_GRANT_TTL_SECONDS` | `86400` by default (60 to 2592000). How long the grant issued to an admitted run lasts. |
| `CALIBER_APPLY_REQUIRE_DISTINCT_APPROVER` | `false` by default (a single-operator or development install keeps applying its own candidates); required `true` under `CALIBER_PROFILE=reference`, which refuses to start without it (`apply_distinct_approver_disabled`) and enforces the rule at request time even so. The two-person rule for `POST /jobs/{id}/apply`: the account that requested the job (its recorded `triggered_by`) cannot apply its candidate (`403`, `reason_code` `apply_self_approval`), and a job with no recorded requester is refused (`403`, `apply_creator_unknown`) rather than passed. Both are refused before any claim, approval record or promotion, and the claim repeats the check on the row-locked job together with the caller's current project permission and the exact candidate digest recorded by the eval gate; each refusal is audited. See [Apply: a distinct approver](m-64-reference-profile.md#apply-a-distinct-approver-b063-747) and [Apply: the claim rechecks everything](m-64-reference-profile.md#apply-the-claim-rechecks-everything-b064-753). |
| `CALIBER_APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS` | `86400` by default (1 to 31536000). How long an approval request bound to an effect proposal stays answerable: its `expires_at` is `requested_at` plus this many seconds, and a request at or past it is refused with the reason code `expired` (see [Approval requests](m-64-reference-profile.md#approval-requests-bound-to-the-exact-intent-b061-706)). Read by the caller that creates the request (`configured_ttl_seconds`); a change affects only requests created afterwards. |
| `CALIBER_RULE_BUNDLE_PATH` | Empty by default. Path of the rule bundle every admitted run is pinned to; set together with `CALIBER_RULE_BUNDLE_SHA256` (one without the other fails startup). Admission verifies the file's bytes against the digest, records the absolute path and digest in the run manifest, and refuses to admit while the file is missing or changed. Each agent step of an admitted run re-verifies the bytes at the *recorded* path against the *recorded* digest and cites the bundle in its context manifest; changed bytes refuse the step (`context_denied` with `rule_bundle_changed`). Changing these settings affects only runs admitted afterwards, and a run whose bundle changed stays failed (resubmit; set path and digest together). The recorded path is the **symlink-resolved** one and must exist with the same bytes on every node that can execute the run (a ConfigMap/Secret `..data/<timestamp>` mount or a Docker secret does not qualify). Use versioned, content-addressed file names and keep the old file until old runs drain. Admission refuses a bundle whose context citation exceeds 256 KiB. See `docs/operate/reference-profile.md`, "The rule bundle at context use". |
| `CALIBER_RULE_BUNDLE_SHA256` | Empty by default. The full lowercase SHA-256 of the rule bundle's exact bytes (see `CALIBER_RULE_BUNDLE_PATH`). |

Optimizer plugins are enabled by a separate allowlist; see [Writing a CALIBER plugin](m-23-sdk-plugins.md).

## 8. Feature flags

Four settings gate the areas the alpha does not stand behind. Three are **off by default**; `CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA`
is the exception and defaults **on**. Each is read once at startup, so restart CALIBER after changing one. A
set variable accepts `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on` (any case) as true and anything else as false (so a typo turns
a flag off, even Aria's); leaving it unset falls back to the field's own default. Each is a
`feature_<id>_enabled` field in `config.py`.

| Setting | Default | What it turns on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA` | `true` | The Aria assistant and plans (preview): the `/assistant/*` and `/aria/*` routes and the Plans page. `CALIBER_ASSISTANT_ENABLED` still decides whether an enabled assistant accepts requests |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS` | `false` | MCP servers and OpenAPI integrations (preview): the `/mcp-servers*` and `/openapi-integrations*` routes and their pages. While it is off, a workflow MCP node is reported as unavailable ("A registered MCP server that CALIBER can reach (needs CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)") |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_COOKBOOKS` | `false` | Cookbooks (preview): the `/cookbooks*` routes and the Cookbooks page. A lab can need another flag as well; its README says which |
| `CALIBER_FEATURE_RELEASE_CANDIDATES` | `false` | Release-candidate signoff and workspace releases (record-only and experimental): the `/releases/candidates*`, `/releases/report-jobs*` and `/projects/{id}/releases*` routes and the candidate UI. The live board, the timeline and release operations are core and always on |

While a flag is off, every route of its area answers HTTP 404 with `reason_code: feature_disabled`, and the web
app hides the area's navigation entries. `GET /capabilities` reports all four under `features` (`enabled`,
`env_var`, `label`, `stability`). In the Docker Compose stack the four variables pass through from the
environment with the same defaults; `.env.example` documents them. See
[Feature flags](m-61-alpha-scope.md#feature-flags) for what changing one means.

## 9. Secret-source convention

Prefer settings ending in `*_SOURCE` for credentials and sensitive values. The
current runtime is designed around secret sources rather than spreading literal
keys throughout deployment files.
